extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of theatre history, biography, and 19th-century American cultural history
extracted.subtask_description: A full-length 19th-century biography of the American actor Edwin Forrest that combines narrative life-history with moral and philosophical commentary on the drama and the actor's place in national culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical-history plan for biography
rubrics_metrics.description: “The plan of the ensuing biography is that of a philosophical history, which adds to the simple narrative of events a discussion of the causes and teachings of the events.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorial approach: do not limit the work to mere chronology; supplement life events with analysis of causes, lessons, and wider meanings. The Prefatory Note explicitly frames the book as combining narrative with interpretive, didactic material to derive moral values from the subject's life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interspersing narrative with general studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer has "interspersed the mere recital of personal facts and incidents with studies of the principal topics of a more general nature intimately associated with these, and has sought to enforce the lessons they yield."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural recommendation: alternate episodes of personal anecdote with thematic essays on larger topics connected to the subject (e.g., dramatic art, friendship, fame) so the biography gains both descriptive interest and moral/philosophical value. Readers uninterested in disquisitions may skip them, implying optional depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and freedom from sectarian/partisan bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Biography should be written with "a free and universal standard" and "stooping to no meaner considerations than the good and evil, the baseness and grandeur of man as man," avoiding "narrow distastes, class and local biases."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard: the biographer must cultivate liberal appreciation and avoid letting sectarian, partisan, clique, or local prejudices distort judgments. Courage to state honest convictions is encouraged despite possible public disfavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain authorial motive where unconventional (transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because "there is still lingering...a strong prejudice against the dramatic profession" and the author is a clergyman, he states it "is not inappropriate ... to state the circumstances and motives which caused him to undertake it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethos guidance: if the writer’s background or perspective might surprise readers (e.g., a clergyman writing an actor's life), include an explanatory preface to provide the proper key and cue to the work rather than a defensive apology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection: criteria for a life worth writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The author argues the subject must "live largely and deeply and shown bold and exalted qualities" and that the biography should present "the fortunes of his kind" for thoughtful readers seeking improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection metric: prioritize subjects whose lives are rich in experience, moral or intellectual lessons, public significance, or exemplify broader social or artistic developments—rather than 'lives of nobodies.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of first-hand acquaintance and primary testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Author recounts having many personal meetings with Forrest in which "he without restraint unpacked his soul" and thus draws on direct interviews and confidences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological preference: rely on direct interviews, personal confidences, and primary testimony when possible; disclose the nature and extent of personal access to justify interpretive claims and intimate detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness: write while data and witnesses remain available
rubrics_metrics.description: "The historic place and power of Forrest are of themselves one good reason why his life should be fully and fairly written while all the data are within reach."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical criterion: documentary materials, eyewitnesses, and contemporary records diminish over time—author recommends composing biographies promptly while sources remain accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for an actor's historic rank
rubrics_metrics.description: Forrest's claim to be "the first great original American actor" rests on "his nativity, the variety, independence, vigor, and impressiveness of his impersonations, the important parts with which he was so long exclusively identified, the extent and duration of his popularity, and the imposing results of his success."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative checklist for theatrical rank: consider nativity/national identity, stylistic originality, range of roles, energetic/expressive qualities, long-term identification with key parts, geographic reach and duration of popularity, and measurable outcomes (financial success, cultural impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance popular verdict and expert criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: While competent critics can detect fine merit, the author defends popular judgment: sustained, widespread democratic tribute over decades is evidence of substantial merit—"a wide, solid, and permanent reputation...is obtained only by substantial merit of some kind."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical stance: weigh both trained critical opinion and broad public reception; long-term, nationwide popular acclaim is a legitimate indicator of significance and should not be lightly overruled by specialist tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve performances by vivid description
rubrics_metrics.description: The tragedian "has no chance" to be remembered unless "the features and accents of the great characters he created are photographed in breathing description on the pages that record his triumphs and make him live forever."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archival/aesthetic aim: a good theatrical biography should attempt to recreate stage performances in writing—detailed, vivid description of roles, manner, voice, gesture—to transmit the actor's art to future readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest portrayal of virtues and faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Author acknowledges Forrest's "undeniable faults...frequent outbreaks of harshness and fierceness...a vein of unforgiving bitterness" but insists the man was "grand and sweet" at core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical guideline: include both admirable qualities and serious faults candidly; showing penalties and consequences of errors adds moral instruction and credibility to the biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use biography to illustrate larger lessons about the art and society
rubrics_metrics.description: The life should be used "to show what are the elements of good and bad acting...to contrast the folly of living to gain applause with the dignity of living to achieve merit...to expose the mean and malignant artifices of envy, jealousy, and ignoble rivalry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thematic objective: leverage an individual life as a case study to illuminate broader questions—artistic standards, professional ethics, social attitudes toward theatre—and to teach ideals of life and criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray inner structure and physical/psychological constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Author analyzes Forrest's "massive physique, his powerful personality...the slowness of his action...the organic foundation...the unification of the nervous system" as explanatory of his stage power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical technique: include physiognomic, temperamental, and psychological analysis (gesture, voice, bearing, nervous organization) when relevant to explain artistic gifts and public effect; tie physical/psychic traits to performance style.
